topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Etiological factors and epidemiological patterns in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how stochastic mutations, genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures interact to drive cancer risk and shape global variations in incidence.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental carcinogens, mutational damage, and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how specific agents induce carcinogenesis through molecular pathways ranging from direct DNA adduct formation to metabolic activation and inflammatory tumor promotion.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and assessing exposure risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and evaluate practical exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the final summary of the core lecture themes and concluding remarks.
